transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, what brings me in is that my head just feels really foggy lately. I've been making these little mistakes in my client notes at work, and... I keep forgetting what I was just about to do. It's really not like me to be this scattered, so I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
How has your sleep been lately—are you having any trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested when you wake up?

Well, my sleep has been kind of all over the place lately. Sometimes I just lie in bed thinking about family stuff and have a hard time actually falling asleep. Or, other times, I'll wake up way before my alarm goes off, and I just can't really settle back down to get any more rest. So yeah, it hasn't been great.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you'd normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Lately, I've been waking up with this... heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I mean, I can still get through my shift and talk to people just fine, but inside, I just feel really sad and flat most of the time.
How long have you been feeling this way—the low, flat mood and the foggy thinking—has it been going on for a couple of weeks, or longer?
It's been going on for a while now. I'd say that low, empty feeling, along with the fogginess... it's been hanging over me for about a month.
Aside from the low mood, would you say you've been worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, health, or family—and finding it hard to control or stop that worry?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, I have regular stress like anyone else, and sometimes my mind wanders to family stuff at night like I mentioned earlier, but I'm not excessively worrying about everything. It's not like my thoughts are out of control or anything. It's really just that low, empty feeling more than feeling anxious or worried.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?

No, not really. I still like doing my regular stuff. I mean, I still hang out with my friends and keep up with things I like to do... I just feel kind of down while I'm doing them, I guess. But I wouldn't say I've lost interest or stopped enjoying them altogether.
Before this past month, had you ever gone through longer stretches—maybe lasting a year or more—where you generally felt down or low most of the time, even if it wasn't this intense?
No, I don't think so. I've never really had a long stretch like that where I felt down for a whole year or anything. This past month has been pretty new for me. Usually, my mood is just normal.
Have you ever had a period of several days where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, along with increased activity or impulsivity?

Yeah, actually. Right before I got this low, I did have a stretch like that. I felt... I don't know, almost too good. Like I felt really powerful one minute, but then the next, I’d get really sharp with my wife or snap at my coworkers over really small things. So, yeah, I guess I did experience something like that.
How many days in a row did that period of feeling unusually energetic or 'too good' and irritable last?
I'm not really sure exactly how many days it was. It's hard to remember the exact number, to be honest. It just felt like a stretch of time before I started feeling down like this.

Thinking back to that time, can you recall any specific events—like a weekend, a work week, or something on your calendar—that might help you figure out whether that high-energy, irritable stretch lasted at least four days in a row?

I'm trying to think back... but honestly, no. I really can't tie it to anything specific on the calendar. My work schedule is pretty much the same every week, so the days just kind of run into each other. I really can't say for sure if it was four days in a row or not. That whole stretch is just kind of a blur of being really wound up before I crashed.
During that time when you felt unusually energetic and irritable, did your wife or coworkers say anything about noticing a change in you?

I don't think so. I mean... nobody actually said anything to me about it. Like I mentioned, I know I snapped at my wife and a couple of people at work, but they didn't really point out that I was acting differently or anything like that. If they noticed a big change, they didn't bring it up to me.
During that stretch when you felt unusually energetic and irritable, did you find you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt rested and full of energy?

Yeah, actually. For a few nights there, I think I was only getting maybe three or four hours of sleep. But the weird thing was, I didn't feel tired at all. I'd wake up feeling completely charged and ready to go. I'd still make my morning coffee, but it was really just out of habit, not because I actually needed it to wake up.

During that energetic, irritable stretch, did you find yourself doing things differently than usual—like taking on more tasks, spending money more impulsively, or starting new projects you wouldn't normally jump into?

Yeah, I definitely did. I was taking on a lot. Um, I was pushing really hard on all these different plans at once. Like, I was trying to sort out memorial details, getting some car repairs done, looking into CNA classes, and even coming up with new business ideas. Just trying to do all of it at the exact same time. 

I also noticed I was calling my relatives and coworkers a lot more than I normally would. So yeah, I was definitely doing things a bit differently.
Do you recall if that energetic, irritable stretch was still going on by the time your next scheduled day off from work came around?
I'm honestly not sure. I mean, it's hard to remember exactly when it started and stopped. I just know it lasted for a few days, but I couldn't tell you if it bled into my next day off.

Thinking about the tasks you mentioned—sorting memorial details, car repairs, looking into CNA classes—can you recall how many separate workdays or shifts you went through while you were in that keyed-up, high-energy state?

I really couldn't give you an exact number. I work pretty regular shifts, but when I get like that, the days just kind of blur together. I know I went to work, but I couldn't tell you if it was two shifts or four shifts while all that was going on. It's just hard to pin down the exact timeline.

During that energetic, irritable stretch, did it cause any real problems—like conflicts at work, trouble completing tasks properly, or anyone needing to step in—or were you still able to function pretty normally despite feeling that way?

No, I didn't really have any major problems. I mean, I was definitely irritable and doing a lot, but it didn't mess up my work or anything. I was still getting my job done, and nobody had to step in or talk to me about my behavior. I was functioning fine, just... running a lot hotter than usual, I guess you could say.
